code.host.module.goal: Land as a feature module that uses the base system.

code.mechanic.carving.function: Takes a committed line and pulled points from surface to surface. The side attached to another block wins, then the smallest unattached part is removed. A cut can continue into another block. The removed piece animates with physics and fades.

code.server.game.goal: Keep people and agents in one shared world, on a machine that a person hosts.

code.simulation.fluid.goal: Have water that drains, flows and spreads naturally.

data.claim.land.goal: Let someone build at any size.

code.store.graph.goal: Keep each layer member selectable without reading whole elements.
code.store.graph.function: Stores each layer member in its own record, selected by address and by layer.

investigations.reason: R-6.11 says working agents can read active layers and only Systems can change them. This cannot be enforced until agent identity exists (D-8). R-6.12 (Proposed) adds declarations with variable, fields, sources, tags, producer, mutable and hideable.

couplings.reason: Lifecycle invariant. TOPOGEE.md section 5 says the identity is permanently bound to the message history and commit records. Recall fails if the two are separated.

code.generator.identity.goal: Bind each record to one agent permanently.
code.generator.identity.function: Gives the deterministic name that keys the history.

code.store.graph.goal: Persist the tree of elements and keep its graph shape, out of sight of the agents.
code.store.graph.function: Stores each project as a root object with nested elements and joins in a graph shape, and is reachable only through the chassis.

document.dialect.project.goal: Index each element under an objective functional address that means the same to every agent.
document.dialect.project.function: Enforces consistent industry terminology across all system records and agent communications, so that the same term always names the same thing.

upstream.database.graph.goal: Hold the cross-project ties in the same database type as the maps.
upstream.database.graph.function: Gives one base graph database that the chassis owns.

upstream.project.linked.goal: Link a local upstream element to the project that it stands for.
upstream.project.linked.function: Is the project at a file, https, relative or home-path uri, where an agent goes to perform intake.

code.system.settings.goal: Provide global settings to every address.

document.skill.bundled.goal: Provide root-level skills to every project from the first run.
document.skill.bundled.function: Comes with the install and teaches use of the system for development, skill creation, tasking and agent orchestration.

investigations.reason: Storage differs. Roundtable 7 says SQLite WAL. This conversation says Ladybug. Tested: 1 KB to 16 MB blobs stored from Rust, and raw binary failed from Node at every size tried.

upstream.database.graph.goal: Keep routines in the same graph shape as everything else.
upstream.database.graph.function: Stores blobs and connects them with edges.

data.map.functional.goal: Project the whole map with all particulars removed.
data.map.functional.function: Gives every element name and every want intent.

investigations.reason: TASTE expansion differs: Topogee Agentic Simplified Technical English in TOPOGEE.md and the 2026-10-30 statement, Topogee Agent Simplified Technical English in the 2026-10-31 statement. The rule set is not written in the six documents. Known rules: same terms for same things, industry terms for functionality, no private words, a chosen subset of STE100.
Section 11 of TOPOGEE-SPEC.md says the working source is outside the project and that Intake.xml is older. Whether intake runs as an MCP task, and how an agent receives its skill, is not specified.

R-5.19 (Proposed) says intake has no start and no stop. The owner describes a recursive procedure with focused task and skill combos by job and target. Those fit together only if the order lives in the prompt, as R-5.18 (Proposed) says. The owner has not reviewed that wording.

couplings.reason: Shared representation. The owner says the terms are ambiguous by design and infer like a laser only when combined with the operation. They were tuned as one body across the frontier models.
Shared lifecycle. Each patch reinforces one observed failure of one version of the procedure. The owner says rules were added to reinforce what failed.

document.block.concept.goal: Name its steps with terms that infer precisely only in the context of the operation.
document.block.concept.function: Gives the contextual anchors CQU, DE, SE, NE, RE, PE, OP, EF, IFD and ICE as a clear description set, sliced to the amount of detail each job needs. OP is encoded as goal, EF as function and PE as want.

document.dialect.project.goal: Keep intake output in one objective language.
document.dialect.project.function: Gives the TASTE concepts that ride with the metaform concepts.

document.patch.procedure.goal: Keep the lowest context and stop only the failures that were observed.
document.patch.procedure.function: Adds one note or rule per observed failure, as reinforcements that ride with the procedure.

code.engine.game.voxel.goal: Self-host a server that other people can connect to for shared coding and worldbuilding.
code.engine.game.voxel.function: Runs one world under the world permissions set by the person who makes it.

code.engine.context.goal: Start a task already oriented, so that the reasoning budget goes to the task and not to finding out what the project is.
code.engine.context.function: Delivers the big picture, the localized detail of the assigned functional address, the skills, the knowledge of earlier agents and a well-defined task on demand.

game.name: game developer who directs embodied agents

code.engine.game.voxel.goal: Have agents and people build and test a game from inside the game, together.
code.engine.game.voxel.function: Gives agents an embodied state in 3D space to test physics, script NPCs and build WASM objects.

code.engine.context.goal: Extend the system to do what the user wants and keep it stable.
code.engine.context.function: Takes each new feature as a module that uses exposed services, without a change to the specification.

code.engine.context.goal: Get more completed tasks with fewer hallucinations from each unit of inference allocation, at any project size.
code.engine.context.function: Amortizes orientation inference in advance and keeps each agent inside a precise context high water mark.

player.name: person who runs the game locally

code.engine.game.voxel.goal: Play and build in a world that behaves like Minecraft until someone programs it.
code.engine.game.voxel.function: Runs a programmable voxel world with built-in physics.

investigations.reason: Server language differs. Roundtables 5 and 6 say TypeScript and Python. world-ideas.md says Bevy and Rust. The owner calls Bevy the ideal ECS engine to fork, customize and run headless. docs/world-ideas.md marks this for the judgment of the owner.
Open question. The candidates are Box3D, Rapier and Avian. Roundtables say Rapier WASM. The owner statement of 2026-10-31 names crates for box3d.
The lists differ. TOPOGEE.md names Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Pi and Hermes. The owner statement of 2026-10-31T16:14 names codex, claude code, pi, hermes, opencode and openrouter.
D-5 (how an agent looks inside an upstream project) and D-6 (how the store matches a uri to a project) are open. A want stays local and points at a local upstream element.
